verdict: A thin day: mostly arXiv research chaff and studio-of-the-week press releases, with one real production tool item (Enscape for Revit) and little else that changes what to do this week.

stories.headline: Enscape adds real-time rendering plugin workflow guide for Revit BIM users
stories.body: Chaos published a workflow guide for Enscape running as a live plugin inside Revit, covering what to configure before client walkthroughs and how the integration behaves during a design review. This is adjacent to VFX work but relevant where studios touch BIM/AEC visualization pipelines or use Enscape-adjacent real-time tools. No new version or licence change mentioned, just workflow documentation from Chaos.
stories.why: Useful reference if the studio ever touches real-time BIM visualization work alongside VFX.

stories.headline: Flow Studio adds a 3D Editor for staging characters, CG worlds and cameras
stories.body: befores & afters covered a new 3D Editor feature in Flow Studio that lets users stage scenes with characters, CG environments and controllable cameras, described as a director's-seat tool. Details are thin, this reads as a vendor feature announcement rather than a technical breakdown, and it's unclear what engine or export path underlies it.
stories.why: Worth a glance if Flow Studio is already in the pipeline, but no technical detail to act on yet.

stories.headline: I turned myself into a pig with AI [Free & Local VFX Tutorial]
stories.body: The demonstration of MiniMax-H3's ability to handle multiple conditioning inputs (original video performance, character reference sheets, audio, and timed prompt cues) in a single pass to perform high-fidelity character replacement.
stories.why: This workflow functions as a high-end neural rendering pass. In a USD/Houdini pipeline, it would sit post-animation/lighting as a 2D replacement tool or be used in early pre-viz for realistic performance evaluation without full 3D rigging. It bridges the gap between 2D plate editing and 3D character integration.

whats_transferable: Timed Emotion Cues: Embedding timestamps directly into text prompts to synchronize AI-generated expressions with the source video performance.
Character Sheet Conditioning: Using a grid of character views/emotions as a reference image to maintain identity across video frames.
Inpainting for Plate Preservation: Restricting the AI model to a specific mask to keep the original background and body movements intact while swapping only the head.
SAM-to-Video-Pipeline: Integrating Segment Anything Model to automatically generate masks for complex objects (like head-mounted camera rigs) for removal.

stories.headline: 3-Step Workflow To Master AI Realism (Full Tutorial)
stories.body: Higgsfield SeeDream 5.0 Pro and Seedance 2.5 release, focusing on cinematic consistency through 'blocking maps' and location-anchored prompting.
stories.why: Currently a proprietary, web-hosted ecosystem. While it doesn't ingest USD directly, the method of using schematic blocking maps to drive prompt-spatial awareness is highly applicable to any multi-character generative workflow.

Employing 'character-back wipes' to hide temporal discontinuities between AI video cuts
